utterance: Good afternoon Daniel, I'm Dr. — glad you could come in. I see you hurt your back over the weekend and booked as urgent, so let's get you looked after properly. Can you walk me through exactly what happened when it started, and what your back has been like since then?
reply: It happened on Saturday when I was lifting a big pot plant in the garden and felt a twinge. Then I woke up on Sunday and could barely get out of bed, so it has been about three days now. I was hoping we could arrange an MRI to see if I have a slipped disc.

utterance: Thanks for that. I'll be straight with you — most injuries like this settle well without an MRI, and I'll explain why in a moment. But first I need to rule out the things that do need urgent attention. Does the pain go down into your buttock or leg at all? If so, how far — above the knee, below the knee, or into your foot? Do you have any numbness, tingling or weakness in either leg or foot?
reply: No, nothing down my legs at all, and my legs feel completely normal.

awards.label: Whether the pain spreads down the legs
Red flag excluded: Weakness, numbness or pins and needles in the legs

utterance: Good, that's reassuring. Now the most important screening questions: have you noticed any problems with your bladder — trouble starting, leaking, or anything unusual? Any numbness around your back passage or genitals — the "saddle" area? And any changes in your bowels, like accidents or difficulty passing them?
reply: All of that is completely normal, and I haven't noticed anything like that.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Any change in passing urine — difficulty, retention or leaking
Red flag excluded: Numbness around the buttocks, genitals or back passage
Red flag excluded: Any loss of bowel control

utterance: Great. A few more quick checks: any fevers, chills or drenching night sweats? Any unexplained weight loss? Have you ever had cancer, or ever taken steroid tablets for more than a few weeks? And is the pain worst at night when you're lying still, or mainly when you move and bend?
reply: No fevers or infections, and if anything I have put some weight on. I have never had cancer or taken steroid tablets like that. It hurts when I roll over, but once I'm settled I sleep, and it is worse when I bend or get out of a chair, better lying still with a heat pack, and worse by the evening.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Fever or recent infection
Red flag excluded: Unexplained weight loss
Red flag excluded: Any history of cancer
Red flag excluded: Steroid use
Red flag excluded: Pain at night or at rest that keeps him awake

utterance: That sounds like a classic mechanical strain. On a scale of 0 to 10, how bad is the pain right now, and what has it been like at its worst? Have you had back pain like this before? And have you taken anything for it so far — and does anything help?
reply: It is about a seven when I move or roll over, but maybe a three if I keep still. I tweaked it once maybe five years ago, but it was gone in a week. I have just taken some paracetamol, but honestly, it did not do much.

utterance: Your legs look fully normal — strong, normal reflexes, full sensation, and no nerve irritation — which is reassuring. One last safety question: any history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney problems, or asthma — anything that would rule out anti-inflammatories like ibuprofen? And do you take any blood-thinners?
